module_title: Advent of Europeans - Cartaz System, Carnatic Wars, and British Supremacy
introduction: This advanced level analyzes Portuguese naval hegemony (the Cartaz system), the strategic details of the Anglo-French rivalry (causes and treaties of the Carnatic Wars), the 'Magna Carta' farman, and the micro-level reasons for the British EIC's triumph over the French.

core_concepts.title: Cartaz-Armada-Cafila System
core_concepts.description: The Portuguese established naval supremacy in the Arabian Sea using a permit system called 'Cartaz'. Any Asian or Arab ship had to purchase a pass and pay taxes to the Portuguese to navigate these waters. Even Mughal Emperor Akbar had to acquire a Cartaz.

core_concepts.title: The Carnatic Wars (1746-1763)
core_concepts.description: These three wars were essentially an extension of the Anglo-French rivalry in Europe. The 1st war (linked to the Austrian War of Succession) ended with the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle; the 2nd war (local succession disputes) ended with the Treaty of Pondicherry; and the 3rd war (linked to the Seven Years' War) ended with the Treaty of Paris.

core_concepts.title: Farrukhsiyar's Farman (1717) - The Magna Carta
core_concepts.description: Mughal Emperor Farrukhsiyar issued a farman to the British envoy John Surman. For an annual payment of Rs 3,000, the EIC got duty-free trade rights in Bengal (Dastak) and permission to mint their own coins. British historian Orme called it the 'Magna Carta' of the Company.

core_concepts.title: Reasons for British Success
core_concepts.description: 1. The British EIC was a private company with quick decision-making, while the French company was state-controlled and delayed. 2. The British Navy was superior. 3. The British had three strong bases (Calcutta, Bombay, Madras) against the sole French base (Pondicherry). 4. The conquest of Bengal (1757) provided the British with immense wealth to fund their wars.

important_entities.name: Captain Best
important_entities.significance: He defeated the Portuguese naval fleet at Swally Hole (near Surat). This impressed Jahangir so much that he granted the English permission to establish a factory at Surat.

important_entities.name: Francois Martin
important_entities.significance: In 1673, he acquired a village from the Subedar of Valikondapuram and developed it into Pondicherry, which became the nerve center of the French in India.

important_entities.name: Dr. William Hamilton
important_entities.significance: He was part of the John Surman mission and cured Emperor Farrukhsiyar of a painful disease. This played a huge role in the Emperor happily granting the 1717 Farman.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Farrukhsiyar granted the 'Dastak' (Free Pass) specifically for 'Company trade'. However, British officials misused it to exempt their 'private trade' from taxes. This massive revenue loss for Bengal became the primary trigger for the Battle of Plassey (1757).

The 'Carnatic Wars' were not fought in the modern-day Indian state of Karnataka. Historically, the 'Carnatic' referred to the Coromandel coast and its hinterland (modern-day Tamil Nadu and parts of Andhra Pradesh).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: 1st War: Aix-la-Chapelle (1748), 2nd War: Pondicherry (1754), 3rd War: Paris (1763).

exam_strategy_tips: Matching the Carnatic Wars with their corresponding treaties and immediate causes is a favorite question in UPSC and State PCS exams.
Pay attention to Assertion-Reasoning questions regarding the structural differences between the British (Private) and French (State-owned) East India Companies.
